title: Fare Thee Honey Blues — Mamie Smith & Her Jazz Hounds (1920)
lyrics:
My baby has left me, I don't know what I'll do
Now every day I've been here, it makes me feel so blue
I'm leaving here today, and that is why

I'm leaving town to wear you off my mind
I've been mistreated and I don't mind dying
I'll buy me a ticket as long as my right arm
I'll ride so far you'll think I'm dead and gone

I'll find me a man, just as long as I'm home
If you don't want me, why don't you tell me so

I can get a friend most anywhere I go
There's a place in Georgia, a change is in the middle of me
I don't want nobody that don't want me
Don't you leave me here
direction: A rented room and a small-town railway station, 1920, late afternoon into dusk; hand-tinted 35mm, no modern objects

treatment.title_treatment: I’ll keep this farewell inside a rented room and a small-town railway station in 1920, letting late afternoon sink into dusk through hand-tinted 35mm, worn amber and bruised blue, with no modern objects or visible text. Our fictional traveler moves from abandonment toward stubborn self-possession; twelve-second takes stretch across eight-bar scenes so a packed bag, an empty chair and a waiting platform carry the blues without melodrama.

cues.cue: Bar 1 opening — hold the rented room for eight bars, extending its first frame beneath the opening pickup.
cues.shot: Wide, slow dolly into a modest rented room in 1920 late afternoon: a fictional woman in a plain period traveling dress stands beside an open leather valise and an empty wooden chair, amber window light crossing the floor. Hand-tinted 35mm with gentle gate weave; a twelve-second take slowed over eight bars, no modern objects, no visible text and no facial close-ups.

cues.cue: Bar 6 lift — breathe two soft amber swells across one bar, like sunlight escaping a cloud.

cues.anchor: Bar 9 instrumental continuation, leading into the first vocal at bar 14
cues.cue: Bar 9 — move behind her shoulder for eight bars; let the first admission arrive against the empty chair.
cues.shot: In the same rented room in 1920 late afternoon, track slowly behind the fictional traveler as she lifts a second teacup, hesitates and leaves it beside the empty chair, her face turned away. Amber-edged shadows and muted blue hand-tint on textured 35mm; twelve seconds slowed across eight bars, period objects only, no text or facial close-ups.

cues.anchor: Bar 17 low passage before the bar 18 lift and bar 22 departure lyric
cues.cue: Bar 17 — watch her fold the last dress for eight bars; at the departure line, the valise closes.
cues.shot: A waist-level lateral move through the rented room in 1920 late afternoon follows the fictional woman's hands folding a worn dress into a leather valise, then pressing its lid shut with restrained resolve. Hand-tinted 35mm, amber window light and blue shadows; a twelve-second take deliberately slowed over eight bars, no modern objects, text or facial close-ups.

cues.anchor: Bar 22, 'I'm leaving here today, and that is why'
cues.cue: Bar 22 departure line — widen the amber doorway wash over three bars without a flash.

cues.anchor: Bar 25, preceding the leaving-town lyric in bar 26
cues.cue: Bar 25 — cut to the station for eight bars, letting her small figure carry the leaving-town refrain.
cues.shot: Wide tracking view along a small-town railway station platform in 1920 late afternoon: the same fictional woman walks with her valise past unmarked wooden benches toward a ticket window, shoulders tired but stride purposeful. Low amber sunlight, hand-tinted 35mm and a twelve-second take slowed across eight bars; no signs, lettering, modern objects or facial close-ups.

cues.anchor: Bar 33, leading into the ticket lyric in bar 34
cues.cue: Bar 33 — frame the ticket-window exchange for eight bars, keeping the transaction wordless and the paper hidden.
cues.shot: At the small-town railway station in 1920 late afternoon, a medium side-on dolly follows the fictional traveler sliding coins beneath an unmarked wooden ticket grille; a clerk passes a folded paper directly into her closed glove so no printed surface appears. Hand-tinted 35mm, fading amber light and cool interior shadows; twelve seconds slowed across eight bars, no visible text, modern objects or facial close-ups.

cues.anchor: Bar 34 beat 2, approximate landing of 'I'll buy me a ticket as long as my right arm'
cues.cue: Bar 34 ticket line — give the counter one bar of warm light, a small purchase of possibility.

cues.anchor: Bar 41 loudness lift to 0.55, followed by the ride-so-far lyric in bar 43
cues.cue: Bar 41 lift — open the platform depth for eight bars as the ride-so-far line approaches.
cues.shot: At the small-town railway station in 1920, the last late-afternoon light catches rails beyond the platform while the fictional traveler stands in rear three-quarter silhouette with her valise; slowly retreat to make the empty distance expand around her. Hand-tinted 35mm in dusty amber and slate blue, twelve seconds slowed over eight bars; no modern objects, visible text or facial close-ups.

cues.cue: Bar 44 peak — swell the platform's amber edge once per beat for one bar, soft rather than theatrical.

cues.anchor: Bar 49 instrumental continuation before the companion stanza
cues.cue: Bar 49 — hold a station-bench tableau for eight bars; she makes room without surrendering her bag.
cues.shot: In the small-town railway station waiting room in 1920 as late afternoon approaches dusk, the fictional woman shifts her valise from a wooden bench to her feet while another fictional traveler pauses at the far end; a slow lateral camera move preserves the space between them. Hand-tinted 35mm, weak amber window light and blue corners, twelve seconds slowed across eight bars; no text, modern objects or facial close-ups.

cues.anchor: Bar 57, approximate landing of 'If you don't want me, why don't you tell me so'
cues.cue: Bar 57 questioning line — follow her away from the bench for eight bars, with no backward appeal.
cues.shot: At the small-town railway station in 1920 early dusk, the fictional woman rises from the waiting-room bench and walks through the open doorway onto the platform, the camera following at full-body distance while the other traveler remains seated. Hand-tinted 35mm with receding amber and deepening blue, twelve seconds slowed over eight bars; no modern objects, text or facial close-ups.

cues.cue: Bar 61 dip — let blue dusk replace the amber fill across four bars.

cues.anchor: Bar 65, leading into the friendship lyric near the end of the bar
cues.cue: Bar 65 — allow a quiet act of kindness over eight bars; the destination stays unseen.
cues.shot: On the small-town railway station platform in 1920 dusk, a fictional porter steadies the woman's valise beside a bench and she acknowledges him with a small tilt of her hat; track sideways as pale steam begins drifting beyond the platform edge. Hand-tinted 35mm in slate blue and muted amber, twelve seconds slowed across eight bars; all clothing and objects period-correct, no text or facial close-ups.

cues.cue: Bar 68 fall — withdraw the warm fill for one bar, leaving the figures readable in dusk blue.

cues.anchor: Bar 73, preceding the final refusal and plea in bars 73–75
cues.cue: Bar 73 — hold her resolve and hesitation in one eight-bar approach to the carriage step.
cues.shot: At the small-town railway station in 1920 dusk, an unmarked period passenger carriage stands beside the platform; the fictional woman approaches its open step, grips the handrail and pauses before lifting her valise, seen in a slow full-body push from behind. Hand-tinted 35mm, soft oil-lamp amber against blue steam, twelve seconds slowed across eight bars; no lettering, modern objects or facial close-ups.

cues.anchor: Bar 80 collapse to 0.06 and quiet tail through bar 84
cues.cue: Bar 80 quiet tail — settle into a low blue wash for the final five bars; keep one warm lamp alive.
Bar 81 — finish on the emptied platform for four bars, holding through the last sound.
cues.shot: Locked wide view of the small-town railway station in 1920 dusk: the fictional traveler's skirt and valise disappear inside the stationary unmarked carriage, leaving an empty wooden bench beneath one warm oil lamp as steam thins. Hand-tinted 35mm with blue shadows and amber highlights; an eight-second clip gently slowed through the remaining four bars, no modern objects, text or facial close-ups.
